name: Hydroxypropyl gluconamide

card.summary: A glucose-derived hair ingredient used in bond-repair and strengthening treatments to help damaged, bleached or colored hair look and feel stronger and smoother.
card.note: Usually sold as a blend; supplier claims are the main published description.

quick.overview:
Hydroxypropyl gluconamide is a cosmetic ingredient made by reacting gluconolactone with 3-aminopropanol [2]. It is listed as a humectant and hair-conditioning agent and appears in many bond-repair and 'plex'-style hair products [2].

Its supplier markets it as a glucose-based chemistry for hair strengthening, sold as a blend with hydroxypropylammonium gluconate, to improve strength and manageability of damaged hair [1].
quick.mechanism: According to its supplier, it penetrates into the hair cortex and forms new hydrogen and ionic bonds that support the damaged internal keratin structure [1]. This is the manufacturer's description of the mechanism.
quick.risks: Published safety and performance data are not provided on the ingredient listings consulted. It is a rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic ingredient, and standard product-label guidance applies.

lead: Hydroxypropyl gluconamide (INCI: hydroxypropylgluconamide) is a cosmetic hair-care ingredient made by reacting gluconolactone, a glucose-derived compound, with 3-aminopropanol.[2] It is used in bond-repair and strengthening products so that bleached, coloured or heat-styled hair feels stronger, smoother and easier to manage, which shows up as less breakage and a healthier-looking finish.[1][2]

Its listed functions in the EU cosmetic ingredient database are humectant and hair conditioning.[2] It is best known as part of Fiberhance BM, a liquid supplier blend with hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate marketed by Brenntag as a patented glucose-derived chemistry.[1] The supplier says it penetrates the cortex, forms new hydrogen and ionic bonds that support damaged internal keratin structure, and restores strength and manageability.[1]

Ingredient databases list dozens of bond-building and conditioning products containing it, including items from Bond Bar, OGX, Schwarzkopf Professional, CHI and HASK.[2] The supplier page gives no test results or quantitative data for its claims.[1]

chain: Small glucose-derived molecules enter the hair shaft
Said to form new hydrogen and ionic bonds with damaged keratin
Hair feels stronger and smoother with less breakage after bleaching or colouring
angle.text: The ingredient is added to bond-repair shampoos, conditioners and pre-colour treatments aimed at chemically processed hair. Suppliers describe it as restoring strength and manageability; the effect is on how the hair feels and handles.

infobox: Fiberhance BM blend with hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate (Brenntag)

paras: It appears in bond-building shampoos, conditioners and leave-in or pre-colour treatments aimed at damaged and chemically processed hair.[2] Examples listed by one ingredient database include Bond Bar Bonding Primer, Schwarzkopf Professional Blondme Bond Repair Purple Shampoo, OGX Bond Protein Repair Conditioner, CHI Royal Treatment Bond Repair Conditioner and HASK Shea Butter Conditioner.[2] Fiberhance BM is listed by its supplier for hair care, conditioning-polymer and shampoo formulations; no recommended use level is given.[1]

sections.h: Mechanism as described by the supplier
paras: The supplier describes glucose-derived molecules that enter the hair cortex and form new hydrogen and ionic bonds with the damaged internal keratin structure, supporting strength and ease of management.[1] Brenntag lists two INCI names, hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate and hydroxypropyl gluconamide, with CAS numbers 190445-18-2 and 2060570-71-8.[1]

A 2026 preprint on bioRxiv by Podili and colleagues compared oxidative bleach, sodium hydroxide and formic acid on hair strands and reported reduced stiffness and strength in the bleach- and formic-acid-treated strands; it did not test bond builders.[3]
